assets.title: Isometric / 2.5D
assets.prompt:
Edit this existing Cursed Market concept. Change only the WORLD VIEW camera, scale, and rendering in the room area into a TRUE ORTHOGRAPHIC ISOMETRIC / 2.5D game diorama. The current camera is much too low and cinematic. Use a high three-quarter overhead isometric view, approximately 45-degree yaw and 35-degree downward pitch, parallel perspective, clear visible tabletop and floor, no wide-angle lens, no cinematic depth-of-field. Pull the camera back enough to see the complete compact cutaway appraiser workshop: diamond-like floor footprint, two removed foreground walls, desks, shelves and three portals at the rear. Make the appraiser and orc much smaller, full-body game characters about 12–16% of the screen height, seated/standing across the wooden appraisal desk with the offered Shadow Key between them. Hand-painted low-poly 3D geometry, stylized credible materials, distinguishable full character silhouettes, warm amber work lights and green/plum/cobalt portal accents. This needs to clearly resemble a 2.5D game scene that could be recreated with Three.js, not an illustrated portrait with UI.
Preserve all UI content and its placement: top Cursed Market / Encounter 2/3 / Credit 42 / Energy 7/10 and four players, left Dark Market with Shadow Key 30 and Moon Mirror 24 until encounter end, right Shadow Key appraisal panel Ask 20 / Proposed Value 10 / Risk 20% / Inspect / Appraise / Pass, bottom owned mask/mirror/hourglass and Clear Sight / Shadow Debt. Maintain large readable UI text, consistent thin copper-dark frame style and the original landscape aspect ratio. Keep hidden authenticity and curse unknown. Do not add combat, health bars, brand logos, text paragraphs or new mechanics. Only revise the room's camera and world representation; preserve the gameplay comparison data.

assets.title: Realistic art cards
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: high-fidelity game screen concept, not a functioning screenshot.
Create ONE wide landscape 16:9 game viewport for "CURSED MARKET", a private 2–4-player dimensional-appraiser roguelike. The human player is an appraiser receiving merchandise from dimensional NPCs, not a fighter. This frame is encounter 2 of 3: a tusked orc merchant offers an antique SHADOW KEY over an appraisal counter; the appraisal decision is the main focus. Selected orc portal and two dormant destinations, vampire and autometa, establish the dimensional world without revealing future stock.
Keep the same illustrative information across concepts: top HUD "CURSED MARKET", "ENCOUNTER 2/3", "CREDIT 42", "ENERGY 7/10". Tiny four-player portrait indicators. Main appraisal area "SHADOW KEY", "ASK 20", proposed value "10", "RISK 20%"; three readable actions "INSPECT", "APPRAISE", "PASS". Current goods' hidden authenticity/curse must not be signalled as known by icons or glow.
A compact clearly legible DARK MARKET buy-order area is OPEN, with two wanted goods illustrated as small objects: "SHADOW KEY 30" and "MOON MIRROR 24", and the short line "UNTIL ENCOUNTER END". This is an optional intermittent buyer, not the entire world.
Owned inventory contains a whisper mask, moon mirror, blood hourglass. Two short active-status labels "CLEAR SIGHT" and "SHADOW DEBT" with distinct small authored icons, not emoji. Show appraiser tools such as magnifier, scale or ledger naturally near the key.
The fantasy should feel tense, strange and inhabited, with credit/liquidity choices. Clear visual hierarchy: offered artifact and NPC, appraise controls, current dark-market orders, owned inventory. Restrained concise English UI labels for concept legibility, generous spacing, no text walls, no account/ranking screens, no generic dashboard statistics, no combat/weapons HUD, no marketing poster, no logos/watermark, no mobile device frame. Keep UI labels readable and spell them correctly; do not add lore paragraphs.

Style and medium: a sophisticated card-based appraisal game with photorealistic painted fantasy concept art inside physical-looking artifact and NPC cards. Cards are the primary interaction grammar, not a miniature 3D room. Make a credible tactile wooden appraisal tabletop viewed almost straight-on from slightly above, with a large carefully arranged ORC MERCHANT portrait card and SHADOW KEY artifact card as the central focus. Orc face and hands have realistic tusks, skin texture, weathered clothing and expression; artifact surfaces show rust, engraving and worn metal. Cinematic realism in the card illustrations, composed to read at card size.
Use dark charcoal card grounds, parchment reading areas, restrained copper rules, muted burgundy seal marks. Give cards thin elegant precise frames rather than ornate tangled borders. Three smaller portal destination cards form a tidy upper strip; the main key card has appraisal fields and actions next to it; a separate compact DARK MARKET ledger shows the two buy orders. Player inventory is a clearly readable lower hand of three illustrated cards, with status labels in a small consistent area.
Art quality must be realistic, not cartoon, low-poly or pixel. The result is a believable premium playable card-game interface concept, not a pile of decorative tarot backs, not a casino poker table, and not a generic SaaS card grid. Lighting is warm and cinematic while text and action placement remain clean and usable.

Style and medium: exceptionally crafted authentic 2D pixel-art game screenshot concept, with deliberate discrete pixels, consistent pixel size and crisp nearest-neighbor presentation. Hand-placed-looking 16-bit-era sprites, approximately 32-pixel character proportions, a disciplined limited palette and selective dithering. Top-down / three-quarter overhead tile-based appraiser workshop, not the isometric 3D diorama and not pixel-filtered photorealism. Human appraiser sprite behind desk; expressive orc merchant sprite in front, iron key sprite between them, visible readable room floor, shelves, ledger and luminous portal sprites in the back.
Teal-black shadows, warm candle amber, dusty plum, bone-white type and occasional restrained crimson risk indicators. A lively but uncluttered eccentric fantasy workshop. HUD and appraisal controls use precise rectangular pixel UI with high-contrast legible bitmap-style lettering. A compact DARK MARKET noticeboard on the right lists wanted key and mirror with their actual small pixel sprites. Bottom inventory slots contain the three named item sprites; statuses have simple consistent bespoke pixel icons and short labels. Make the offered key clearly larger in its examination slot and prioritize the player's decision.
No smooth gradients, no depth-of-field blur, no vector-looking rounded cards, no antialiased painterly faces, no 3D render, no blurry enlarged pixels. Avoid generic farming-village imagery. This is a readable inhabited roguelike appraisal game, not a pixel-art wallpaper.
